name: Death Funk
editorial_article:
Death Funk is a specific artistic alias used by the influential German electronic musician Alexander Wilke, better known globally as Alec Empire. Operating primarily during the late 1990s, the Death Funk project served as a specialized outlet for Empire's experimentation with breakbeat-heavy, high-intensity electronic music that aligned with the aggressive, anti-establishment ethos of the Digital Hardcore movement. The alias is most notably associated with the 1997 EP \"Funk Riot Beat,\" which was released on his influential label, Digital Hardcore Recordings (DHR).

As a sonic persona, Death Funk captures a distinct slice of Empire's creative trajectory—one characterized by heavily distorted drums, frantic, hyper-kinetic rhythms, and a total disregard for traditional electronic genre boundaries. While Alec Empire is significantly more recognized for his seminal work with Atari Teenage Riot or his solo industrial productions, the Death Funk project highlights his early career commitment to releasing uncompromising, underground music during a pivotal moment in the development of 90s electronic hardcore. The project remains a significant footnote within the vast DHR catalog, representing the raw, chaotic energy that Empire helped popularize through his various aliases and collaborative endeavors throughout his highly prolific and genre-defying career in the global underground scene. Death Funk is not merely a side project but a testament to the versatility of Empire’s production style, demonstrating how he could condense the fury of his live performances into focused, aggressive studio experiments that challenged the dance music conventions of the mid-to-late 90s. Even today, the releases under this moniker are sought after by fans of early DHR output, reflecting the enduring legacy of the label's commitment to sonic radicalism.
